reference.title: Barbell Half Kneeling Shoulders Press
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the shoulders, breathe out as the bar passes the forehead, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s up, 0.4 s at the top, 2 s down

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen and lighter than a standing press: the half-kneeling base removes the legs. Leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 1-2.5 kg when every rep locks out without arching the back; switch the front leg each set.

cues.text: Right knee down on a pad under the hip, left foot flat in front, both knees about 90 degrees; squeeze the right glute and brace. Bar at the front of the shoulders, hands just outside them, forearms vertical.
Pull the chin back a little and press the bar straight up past the face; head comes through once the bar passes the forehead.
Arms straight, bar over the shoulders and mid-foot of the base, ribs down, no backward lean.
Lower under control to the front of the shoulders, chin back again as the bar passes.
Re-brace at the shoulders before the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to finish the press
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the down-side glute and keep the ribs down; use less weight.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing the bar out in front
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar close to the face and finish over the shoulders.
Brace before each rep and press slower.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Start with the elbows a little in front of the bar.

kinematics.norm: Half-kneeling: down knee under the hip, front shin vertical (common coaching)
Arms close to vertical at lockout (clinical opinion)
From deeply bent at the shoulders to straight (clinical opinion)
Close to the face, finishing over the shoulders; seated and unstable bases change deltoid and core activity (Saeterbakken 2013; Saeterbakken 2012)
Controlled, about 1-2 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Half Kneeling Shoulders Press, video (movement reference only)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

cautions: Use a pad under the down knee.
Clean or lift the bar to the shoulders from a rack set low, not from the floor while kneeling.
Do not arch the lower back to finish the press.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee discomfort: thicker pad, or tall kneeling on both knees.
Shoulder pain: narrower grip, or a half-kneeling single-arm dumbbell press within a pain-free range.
regressions: Seated barbell press with back support.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover lifting the arms overhead (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover lifting the arms overhead (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps raise the arms through the press.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps raise the arms through the press.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straighten the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straighten the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Shrug and rotate the shoulder blades up at the top.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Shrug and rotate the shoulder blades up at the top.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades up so the arms can reach overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades up so the arms can reach overhead.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Upper fibres help start the press from the shoulders.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Upper fibres help start the press from the shoulders.
muscleNotes.core: The narrow kneeling base makes the trunk brace hard against arching and tipping (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist side bending and rotation on the staggered base.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist side bending and rotation on the staggered base.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: The down-side glute squeezes to keep the hip open and the pelvis tucked.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: The down-side glute squeezes to keep the hip open and the pelvis tucked.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on the narrow base.
